summary: Interleaved postback partitioning caused staged credit gap on finalized invoice
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a discrepancy between provisional staged credits (hourly buffer) and the finalized invoice for 2026-02-28. The invoice shows a surplus line item (credits missing) that the customer asserts should have been applied. Impact: Enterprise customer reports +$18,340 unexpected charge on finalized invoice; support hold requested until reconciliation completes. Environment: prod (us-east). Timeline: - 2026-02-28 03:00 UTC: batch postbacks from Stellar Health AI completed. - 2026-03-01 00:15 UTC: customer noticed provisional credits were lower than expected in console. - 2026-03-05 10:42 UTC: final invoice generated showing surplus charge. Observed behavior: Postback aggregator shows a series of out-of-order acknowledgements across partitioned shards; credits for warmup/hourly-buffer were temporarily assigned to a holding ledger and then reconciled to a different tenant tag during a sharded re-aggregation pass. Expected behavior: Credits should be consistently attributed to the originating tenant/org and appear on provisional and final invoices in the same cost center.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate high-volume multi-shard batch postback from a mixed-model job (13b + 7b-quant) with interleaved acknowledgements across partitions.
2) Force a reconciler re-aggregation run (reconciler v2.14 scheduled job) while postbacks are completing.
3) Observe provisional credit allocation in console and compare against post-aggregation ledger entries in billing DB (billing.credits) and invoice generator output.
4) Verify whether credits moved to a holding ledger (ledger_hold) and whether tenant_tag normalization occurred during the re-aggregation window.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Reconciler re-aggregation job (v2.14) can race with in-flight postbacks when partition metadata (tenant_tag) is normalized mid-window, causing credits to be written to ledger_hold and not re-associated before invoice generation.
Hypothesis 2: Partitioned aggregator shards return acknowledgements out-of-order; the merger logic uses last-write wins and the holding ledger TTL expired before re-association in some cases.

Partial finding: Billing exports show ~27 postback batches for tenant 'stellar-prod' moved to ledger_hold between 03:02 and 03:06 UTC. The invoice generator snapshot taken at 03:10 UTC consumed the billing snapshot before the backfill completed.

Dashboards checked: Postback ingestion rate (grafana/INGEST-PBACK), reconciler job overlap heatmap (grafana/RECONCILE-OVERLAP), billing snapshots timeline (grafana/BILL-SNAP). Links: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/POSTBACKS?orgId=1, https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/reconcile/RECONCILE-OVERLAP
Related deploy: normalization patch rolled 2026-02-27 (deploy id deploy-20260227-9). Suspect change to tenant_tag canonicalization triggered more re-aggregations.
resolution: Workaround applied: Manual reallocation of held credits to tenant 'stellar-prod' performed 2026-03-12 12:04 UTC; Finance issued provisional credit memo and invoice amendment queued. Engineering follow-up: reconciler ordering patch (PR referenced) prepared for staging; backfill job scheduled to replay affected postback windows and regenerate corrected invoice lines. Pending items: run backfill to ensure no other tenants affected; add spike alert for reconciler overlap; create postmortem after patch rollout.
